entities.summary: John IV of Saxe-Lauenburg was a Prince-Bishop of Hildesheim. Born in the early 15th century, his ascension to the bishopric in 1506 marked the beginning of a period of significant cultural and religious transformation in the region. As Bishop, John IV oversaw the construction of numerous churches and monasteries, including the iconic St. Michaelis Church in Hildesheim, which became a major pilgrimage site. He also played a key role in the Protestant Reformation in Germany, supporting the teachings of Martin Luther and contributing to the spread of reform within the Holy Roman Empire. John IV's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as his efforts helped shape the religious and cultural identity of the region for centuries to come. The legacy of his patronage can still be seen in the vibrant stained glass windows and intricate carvings that adorn the interior of St. Michaelis Church today.
